newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens up amid selective buy interest.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens up amid selective buy interest.

text.p: Positive market signals and a smattering of good corporate news buoyed German shares at their opening on Thursday, with trading marked by selective buying interest.
The 30-share DAX index, still in a steady bull run, was up 10.18 points at 2,669.15 points in early bourse trade while the December DAX futures contract was up four at 2,682.5.
A slightly firmer dollar and moderate Wall Street gains fuelled the modest gains but dealers said the relatively flat indices masked the strong performance of individual stocks.
"The main thing is to look at specific sectors at the moment," an analyst for ABN Amro Deutschland's research team said.

Pharmaceuticals group Schering's announcement that it might pay a higher than expected two-mark dividend in 1996 helped its shares move 1.95 marks higher to 119.05, while Bayer and Hoechst also edged higher in the chemical sector.
Several banks were trading lower after Moody's Investors Service said it planned to review its ratings of the largest commercial bank in the sector, Deutsche Bank.
Deutsche shares slipped 58 pfennigs to 72.25, while Bayerische Vereinsbank and Dresdner Bank were also lower. "The Moody's news went through the whole sector to some degree," one trader said.
ABN said it saw as more "durable" recent gains in the steel, chemical and car sector compared to those seen by banking stocks, which it said had been mainly based on takeover speculation.
Engineering group Mannesmann gained 5.50 marks to 576 marks after early reports that it would be part of a French telecom consortium including Compagnie Generale des Eaux and British Telecom.

U.S. jobless claims and money supply figures due later in the day are, after the Federal Reserve's decision not to increase rates earlier this week, not seen as having a large impact on German shares.
